I've just run a series of further checks and confirmed it: cells becoming "1" in train 2 are orthogonally isolated; no non-zero neighbors. I just thoroughly tested many examples and there wasn't a single exception. And, for the non-1 cells in train 2, they *all* have at least one non-zero orthogonal neighbor. My confidence is high.


**Verifying Cell Transformations**

I've just applied my neighborhood rule to Train 1 and re-confirmed that every isolated cell became a "1" in the output. I can see the same pattern holds. I have now also verified the transformation on the given test input; the test example also checks out, as I only found one non-zero cell, and it had a neighbor, so it remained zero.
